title: Daikon Dynamic Invariant Detection
description: Daikon watches program executions and reports the properties that always held: x > 0, y == 2*x, array sorted. The invariants are likely, not proven, but they document what the code actually does. Likely invariants guide proof and review.

demo.code:
print("observed over 1000 runs: x > 0, y == 2*x")
print("likely invariant: y == 2*x at loop head")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Daikon', 'invariant': 'Observed properties', 'method': 'Runtime observation', 'strength': 'Likely', 'benefit': 'Documents reality', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'invariant', 'method', 'strength', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Loop Invariant Inference
description: Loop invariants are properties true before and after each iteration, and they are the key to proving loops correct. Inference finds them from the loop body and postcondition. The invariant is the loop's contract with itself.

demo.code:
print("loop: sum array")
print("invariant: s == sum(a[0..i])")
print("proves: final s == sum(a)")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Invariant inference', 'invariant': 'Inductive property', 'method': 'Constraint solving', 'strength': 'Proven', 'benefit': 'Proves loops correct', 'complexity': 'High'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'invariant', 'method', 'strength', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")
